name: violin-jab-music-box
style: cinematic spoken-word sound design cue, no singing, two speaking voices. Opens on a raw hoarse young British man bellowing his words across a rainy late-night taxi rank, drunk, slurred, half-laughing. Instantly after his last word: one savage solo violin stab, bow scraped hard, a single sforzando hit then silence. Then a tiny detuned wind-up music box, a slow three-note loop ticking like a bedside clock, dry and close. Over it a low, warm older woman speaks quietly, unhurried and immovable, like a mother waiting up at the kitchen table. Final seconds: one soft distant car horn melting into a long hall reverb tail. Sparse, intimate, voice-forward mix, rubato, beatless
exclude: drums, percussion, beat, bass drop, sung vocals, melody singing, chorus, choir, rap, autotune, synth pads, EDM, orchestral swell
lyrics:
[Spoken, shouted, drunk young man]
(There's infinite versions of me. One of them gets home fine.)

[Single violin stab]

[Detuned music box loop]

[Spoken, calm older woman, quiet]
(There's only one.)

[Soft distant car horn, reverb tail]
[End]

name: lab-theremin-documentary
style: Spoken-word sci-fi lab cue, 1950s B-movie laboratory, no singing. Warbling theremin glides with wide hand vibrato, oscillator bleeps, a dry Geiger-counter clicking as the only pulse, a glassy synth arpeggio that doubles, triples and detunes into a smeared shimmer, then snaps to one pure sine tone. Two male speakers: a sleepy young British drunk mumbling close to the mic, confiding to himself; a crisp middle-aged British documentary narrator, precise and certain, like a nature presenter naming a specimen. Ends on a heavy car-door thunk, one warm distant car horn and a fading electrical hum. Cinematic short sting.
